body.p: . Replaces 's two XSLT rejection places (reject_schema_awareness's XTSE1660 and XTSE1650 in src/xslt_read.c, , ) with 's mechanisms; golden src/xquery_static.c (import schema), tests/xquery_schema_test.c.

item.p: xsl:import-schema (3.13) is a new module, src/xslt_schema.c (glossary schema_import), run after reading: the declarations of the sealed AST become the documents of one sxml_schema_create (the synthetic schema document): an inline xs:schema as a NODE document of the module's tree (base URI the declaration's), a schema-location as a RESOLVED document resolved against the declaration's static base URI with its namespace checked, a namespace alone as a RESOLVED document by namespace. Of one namespace only the declarations of the highest import precedence count; a namespace a host schema defines (or XSD's) is taken from there; a location or namespace the resolver does not deliver is dropped (3.13: not an error by itself), probed with sxml_schema_scope_probe_document, now shared with XQuery's import schema (one probe, src/schema_scope.c). The processor keeps the schema (sxml_processor_keep_schema, ). XTSE0215 (inline schema with a schema-location or another namespace), XTSE0220 (any schema error, its constraint and description in the message). Schema roles (4.0) are not read: one unnamed role.

In-scope schemas: the host's (static_context.in_scope_schemas of the stylesheet configuration, now read, xslt.h comment, additive), then the imported schema; neither gives the processor's built-in schema. They live in the AST (sxml_xslt_ast_set_in_scope_schemas), the lowering's base static context carries them into every module's XPath static context and IR module and the unit ('s one field), so as types, schema-element(), casts, constructor functions and type-available see them. The host's schemas are what makes a source the host validated and the stylesheet's types the same types (schema types are never interned).

Validation is 's validate row with XSLT's rules: mode SXML_SCHEMA_VALIDATE_MODE_XSLT_RULES (+4) and the descriptor validate-items (item()*): every item validated (documents, elements, attributes) or kept; XTTE1550, XTTE1512, XTTE1510, XTTE1515, XTTE1540, XTTE1555 (a document's cvc-id), XTTE1535. One lowering helper (sxml_xslt_lowering_bind_validation, src/xslt_lower_construct.c) reads [xsl:]validation, [xsl:]type or the default-validation in force and wraps the constructed nodes of xsl:element, xsl:attribute, xsl:copy, xsl:copy-of, xsl:document, xsl:result-document (the result tree's document node), xsl:source-document and literal result elements; preserve is the PRESERVES_TYPES construction flag (XQuery's construction mode), strip the default; XTSE1505 in the reader, XTSE1520 and XTSE1530 at lowering; an unprefixed [xsl:]type is in the default namespace for elements and types. Temporary trees (9.4) are built as preserve (25.2). The evaluator delivers a constructed node into a receiver that preserves types also when the node itself strips (the same tree either way), so variables keep the streaming.

input-type-annotations="strip" (4.1) is the document preparation of whitespace stripping (src/xslt_whitespace.c): the same copy, without annotations, for the global context item and documents fn:doc and document() load.

Typed modes (6.9.4): a mode with typed="yes", "strict" or "lax" (or "no") tries one rule before all its template rules, of the highest precedence and priority, made from two XPath snippets: it matches an item that is not an XNode or an untyped (typed) element or attribute, and its template raises XTTE3100. Name tests are not read as schema-element() (strict, lax; XTSE3105 not raised).
fn:document's xsd-validation option (4.0) validates each document with fn:parse-xml's sxml_schema_scope_validate_document ().

is-schema-aware is true; default-validation strict or lax is XTSE0020 (only preserve and strip are allowed). A schema error whose description already starts with its constraint name is raised without naming it twice (sxml_schema_scope_raise).

XSLT driver: schema_aware is supported but stays a non-goal for scope (outside the denominator, as QT4's schema features, ); a test case requiring it, or whose environment has a schema or a validated source, is counted in the area "schema-aware". The environment's schemas compile into one schema that validates sources (strict, lax) and is the stylesheet's host schema; schema documents are served by suite file and namespace (resource_table.h). Assertions see the namespaces declared inside <result> too (an all-of may declare a prefix).

Not done: typed modes' schema-element() reading of name tests (XTSE3105) and typed="~ItemType"; ID/IDREF is checked when an element (not a document) is validated, where XSLT leaves it to documents (the validator has no switch for it; validation 1601, accumulator-073); xs:untypedAtomic as [xsl:]type; declarations of xml:lang and xml:space (no xml.xsd built in); xsl:copy of an element under preserve keeps its annotation instead of xs:anyType; the fn namespace schema (json-to-xml typed, ); XTSE0265; schema roles.

Measured (release, HEAD 8d6cad4 plus this packet): the schema-aware XT40 area 621 of 971 (64.0 %; feature schema_aware, a schema or a validated source); of the 946 that require schema_aware, the 679 that need no other non-goal (streaming 247, dynamic_evaluation 15, XSD_1.1, dtd, XML_1.1) pass 615 (90.6 %; the proposed gate is 60 %). XT40 8,642 passed (was 7,990; gate rate 8,027 of 8,728 in scope, was 7,990), 560 failed, no test case that passed before fails; XSLT slice 147 of 154; XP40 30,924 and XQ40 41,261 passed, 0 errors; slice 198. Six test cases that asked for schema_aware to be absent no longer run.

Six XT40 errors, all in the schema-aware area and all a source the environment asks to validate that does not validate, reported rather than reclassified: as-3301, as-3401, match-208, match-209 give xs:ENTITY attributes the names of parsed entities (XSD 1.1 Part 2, 3.4.11: an ENTITY names an unparsed entity, so the sources are invalid); catalog-005b and catalog-009 compile XMLSchema.xsd, the schema for schemas, with the catalog's schema, which sxml rejects as sch-props-correct.2 against the built-in components (for 5.13's XSD sweep: whether a schema document for the XSD namespace may restate them).
